chunks.text: | `context-doctor analyze <file>` | Profile a conversation: token breakdown, findings, cost + latency estimates. `--fail-over-budget` exits 1 on a breach, for CI |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text: | `context-doctor optimize <file>` | Apply the safe fixes; add `--strategy trim-tool-calls` for big inline file writes, `--strategy prune-history` for consented lossy compaction |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text: | `context-doctor session [file]` | Profile a Claude Code session: live context, findings, **measured tokens and prompt-cache economics**, **where the wall clock went** per tool, and **what its subagents cost** (their own windows, your bill; never in the parent's profile). Also reads

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text:
ChatGPT data exports (`conversations.json`) |
| `context-doctor init [preset]` | Write a `.contextdoctorrc` from a preset (`chat`, `agent`, `batch`) — a budget you can adopt in one command and tune later |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text:
| `context-doctor experiment --task "…"` | Run one task twice from the same commit, in a fresh session and forked from an `--existing` one, same model and tools; compare bill, cache split, wall clock, and whether `--check` passed. The only command here that spends money, so it caps spend 
per arm and refuses a dirty tree |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text: | `context-doctor diff <before> <after>` | Compare two profiles: what moved by category, which findings were resolved or introduced, and what it saves in money and latency |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text: | `context-doctor accuracy` | How much of what you are billed for is visible in your transcript (the fixed harness baseline, per-turn injected content), plus a tokenizer check: real chars/token per model from the API's own counts, next to the ratio the estimator uses |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text: | `context-doctor cursor [--list]` | Profile a chat from Cursor's local history (both storage formats) |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text: | `context-doctor report` | Machine-wide impact report (proxy savings persist across restarts): exact proxy savings, hook activity, how often the cold-resume `/compact` offer was followed by a compaction, recoverable waste in recent sessions |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text: | `context-doctor proxy` | Always-on local proxy that optimizes every Anthropic/OpenAI API request in flight (`/stats` for cumulative savings) |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text: | `context-doctor watch [file]` | Live monitor of a growing session transcript or agent trace (Claude Code / Codex JSONL, or a plain OpenAI/Anthropic conversation JSON file): token/cost line per change, findings as they appear |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text:
| `context-doctor doctor` | Self-check the whole installation — one pasteable ✓/✗ diagnosis with fixes |
| `context-doctor dashboard` | Local savings dashboard on 127.0.0.1: tokens saved per day, sessions by context in use vs recoverable, budget status |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text: | `context-doctor statusline` | Claude Code status bar: live context vs window, cache share, cost. Wired by `install --statusline`; never overwrites a statusLine you already have |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text: | `context-doctor hook` | The every-prompt Claude Code hook (registered by `install`; you never run this yourself). Warning threshold tunable via `CONTEXT_DOCTOR_WARN_TOKENS` (default 80000) |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > All commands at a glance (cont.)
chunks.text: | `context-doctor-mcp` | The MCP server itself — stdio by default (what the installer wires); `--http [--port 8808] [--host H]` serves streamable HTTP at `/mcp` for URL-based clients like ChatGPT developer-mode connectors |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > What "always-on" means, per surface
chunks.text:
## What "always-on" means, per surface

| Where you run LLMs | Mechanism | Guarantee |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code sessions, with autopilot on | The login-service proxy clears stale tool output from every request, only when the cache is cold | **Every request; never more expensive (measured)** |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > What "always-on" means, per surface (cont.)
chunks.text: | Your own apps/agents (API) | `context-doctor proxy` rewrites every request in flight, or `proxy --autopilot` for the cache-safe mode | **Every call, automatic** |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > What "always-on" means, per surface (cont.)
chunks.text: | Claude Code / Cowork sessions | `install` registers a **UserPromptSubmit hook**: every query measures the session; heavy sessions get injected hygiene guidance (silent when lean, rate-limited, never blocks a prompt) | **Every query checked** |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > What "always-on" means, per surface (cont.)
chunks.text: | Claude Desktop chat / Cursor | **MCP server instructions** — standing hygiene directives injected into every conversation where the server is enabled, plus prescriptive tool triggers | **Every conversation carries the rules** |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > What "always-on" means, per surface (cont.)
chunks.text: | claude.ai (web) / ChatGPT / phone apps | `context-doctor instructions --copy`, pasted once into the account's preferences (or upload `skills/context-doctor/SKILL.md` as a skill) | Every chat on that account carries the rules |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > What "always-on" means, per surface
chunks.text: Without autopilot nothing runs in the background: the hook, skill, MCP server and its instructions are delivered by the apps themselves at the right moment. With autopilot, one small proxy runs as a login service (launchd / systemd user service / logon task) and is restarted by the

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > What "always-on" means, per surface (cont.)
chunks.text: service or by the next prompt's hook if it ever stops.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > What "always-on" means, per surface
chunks.text:
Or use the CLI directly, no install needed:

```bash
npx context-doctor analyze conversation.json --model claude-sonnet-5
```

```bash
npx context-doctor optimize conversation.json --out slimmed.json
```

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > What "always-on" means, per surface
chunks.text:
Input is any of: OpenAI chat format, Anthropic messages format (with `system` and content blocks), or a bare `[{role, content}]` array. Use `-` to pipe from stdin.

Reports include **dollar and latency estimates**, not just tokens:

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > What "always-on" means, per surface
chunks.text:
```
Cost:  ~$3.30 input per call · ~$3302 per 1k calls · ~13.2s of latency per call (estimates)
...
Potential recovery: ~5.9k tokens (~73% of context) ≈ $17.69 per 1k calls, 0.2s faster per call
```

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Profile your actual Claude Code sessions
chunks.text:
## Profile your actual Claude Code sessions

```bash
npx context-doctor session            # profile your most recent session
npx context-doctor session --list    # browse sessions
```

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Profile your actual Claude Code sessions
chunks.text: Parses the transcripts Claude Code writes locally and answers "where did my tokens go today?" — it will happily tell you that one giant skill load is 67% of your context.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean
chunks.text: ## Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean
chunks.text:
```bash
context-doctor autopilot on        # once; survives reboots
context-doctor autopilot status    # what it has done
context-doctor autopilot pause     # instant passthrough, nothing restarts
context-doctor autopilot off       # remove it
```

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean
chunks.text: `autopilot on` runs the local proxy as a background service (launchd on macOS, a systemd user service on Linux, a logon task on Windows), waits until it answers, and only then points Claude Code at it through `env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` in `~/.claude/settings.json`. Every Claude Code

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean (cont.)
chunks.text: session started afterwards in a terminal or an IDE sends its requests through it. **Not the desktop app's Code tab:** it runs Claude Code "host-orchestrated", sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` from its own account configuration, and drops the same key from settings files (checked in Claude Code

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean (cont.)
chunks.text:
2.1.284). `autopilot on`, `autopilot status` and `doctor` look at which surface your recent sessions ran in and warn when autopilot cannot reach them; for desktop sessions the levers that work are the cold-resume advice and `compact-window`. Your login (subscription or API key) passes 
through untouched.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean
chunks.text: **What it does to each request:** once old tool output adds up to 20k+ tokens (file reads, shell output, search and web results, screenshots inside them), it replaces that output with a one-line note, keeping the 3 most recent results. The tool call stays in the history, so the model can

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean (cont.)
chunks.text: simply run it again if it needs the output. Your messages, its answers, answers you gave to its questions, subagent reports and MCP results are never touched.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean
chunks.text: **Why it cannot make a session more expensive.** A prompt cache matches a byte-identical prefix, and changing old history re-bills everything after the change at the write rate (1.25x instead of 0.1x). So autopilot changes history only when the cache is cold anyway: after an idle gap

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean (cont.)
chunks.text:
longer than the cache lifetime the request itself declares (1 hour for Claude Code on a subscription, 5 minutes otherwise), when the whole prompt is re-written regardless. Once cleared, an output stays cleared on every later request, so the prefix is identical between clearings and the 
cache keeps hitting.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean
chunks.text: **Measured before it shipped**, by replaying every Claude Code session on the author's machine (43 sessions, 130 days) request by request through the shipped code, priced as the cache bills it, with real timestamps: 3.8 billion input tokens not sent and $4,694 at list price, ~$1,080 a

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean (cont.)
chunks.text: month ([details](#what-it-saves)). `scripts/replay-autopilot.mjs` does this on yours:

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean
chunks.text:
| Policy | Input cost saved | Worst session |
|---|---|---|
| **Autopilot: clear only when the cache is cold (default)** | **9.8%** (9.2% of raw input tokens; best session 37.7%) | **0.00%, no session worse** |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean (cont.)
chunks.text:
| Also clear on a warm cache when the saving "should" repay the rewrite | 9.9% | −0.13% (one session worse) |
| The proxy's general strategies (dedupe, trim, strip-base64) | 6.7% | −13% (one session worse) |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean
chunks.text: 94% of input cost on that machine came from requests above 200k tokens, which is where the clearing lands. Smaller requests also mean later auto-compaction and a faster first token.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean
chunks.text: **Never in the way:** anything it cannot parse is forwarded unchanged; only Anthropic `/v1/messages` requests are touched. It adds about 7 ms to a 2.9 MB (~1M token) request. If the proxy dies, the service restarts it within seconds, and the every-prompt hook checks it before each prompt

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean (cont.)
chunks.text: and starts it if needed (measured: 0.6 s once, when it had to). `pause` turns it into a passthrough without restarting anything; `off` removes the setting before stopping the service, and sessions started while it was on need a restart.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean
chunks.text: **What it cannot reach** (no process on your machine sends those requests): Claude Desktop's chat tab and claude.ai, which use the standing instructions and the `profile_context` sketch instead; Cursor's own models (Cursor's servers call the model; with your own OpenAI key, see the

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Autopilot: every Claude Code session keeps its own context lean (cont.)
chunks.text: tunnel section below); and Codex signed in with ChatGPT, where the every-prompt hook still reports context size.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically
chunks.text:
## Always-on: optimize every request automatically

Run the proxy and every Anthropic/OpenAI API call your apps make gets optimized in flight — no code changes:

```bash
npx context-doctor proxy
```

Then point your app or SDK at it:

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically
chunks.text:
```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8787      # Anthropic SDKs / tools
export OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8787/v1      # OpenAI SDKs / tools
```

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically
chunks.text:
The proxy dedupes repeated content, trims stale tool results, and strips base64 blobs from the message history of each request, then forwards it to the real API. Your API key passes through in headers untouched, streaming (SSE) works unchanged, and per-request savings are logged with 
upstream latency:

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically
chunks.text:
```
[context-doctor] POST /v1/messages → 200 in 842ms | optimized 7.3k → 518 tokens (2 changes) | session total: 6.9k tokens ≈ $0.021 saved
```

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically
chunks.text: Only conversation requests (`/v1/messages`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`) are ever rewritten. Every other endpoint a client uses through the proxy (listing models, uploading files, counting tokens) is forwarded untouched, to Anthropic when the request carries

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically (cont.)
chunks.text: `anthropic-version` or `x-api-key` and to OpenAI otherwise, and request bodies the proxy does not rewrite reach upstream byte for byte.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically
chunks.text: `GET http://localhost:8787/stats` returns cumulative savings (requests, tokens, estimated USD), **exact upstream usage** read from every response (JSON and SSE), and **prompt-cache advisories** — the proxy watches your real traffic and flags big stable prefixes missing `cache_control` or

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically (cont.)
chunks.text: prefix churn that silently re-bills the cache. Per-model behavior via `--config`: The advisor now says *where*: for a large system/tools prefix it names the block to mark (the last tool definition, or the last system block), and when the older messages were byte-identical to the previous

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically (cont.)
chunks.text: request it names the exact message to put `cache_control` on, with the token count that run is re-billing each turn. Anyone who already placed breakpoints is left alone.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically
context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically
chunks.text: Because prompt caching matches byte-identical prefixes, deterministic strategies are chosen so repeated requests stay stable — but if you rely on aggressive cache prefixes, start with `--strategy strip-base64 --strategy dedupe` and add more as you verify.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically > Putting the proxy on a public URL (Cursor with your own OpenAI key, remote apps)
chunks.text: ### Putting the proxy on a public URL (Cursor with your own OpenAI key, remote apps)

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically > Putting the proxy on a public URL (Cursor with your own OpenAI key, remote apps)
chunks.text: Some apps let you set a base URL but call it from *their* servers, not your machine. Cursor is one: with your own OpenAI key, "Override OpenAI Base URL" is sent to Cursor's backend inside the model configuration, and Cursor's servers make the request (only the key-verification ping is

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically > Putting the proxy on a public URL (Cursor with your own OpenAI key, remote apps) (cont.)
chunks.text: client-side; we checked the app bundle, 3.18.25). So `127.0.0.1` cannot work there; the proxy has to be reachable from the internet, and an open relay on the internet is a bad idea. Hence the token:

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically > Putting the proxy on a public URL (Cursor with your own OpenAI key, remote apps)
chunks.text:
```bash
npx context-doctor proxy --token "$(openssl rand -hex 16)"   # or CONTEXT_DOCTOR_PROXY_TOKEN=...
ngrok http 8787                                               # or any HTTPS tunnel / reverse proxy
```

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically > Putting the proxy on a public URL (Cursor with your own OpenAI key, remote apps)
chunks.text: With `--token`, every path except `/health` must start with `/t/<token>/`; anything else gets 401 before any upstream call, and the comparison is constant time. Then in Cursor: Settings > Models > OpenAI API Key > Override OpenAI Base URL = `https://<your-host>/t/<token>/v1`. Every agent

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically > Putting the proxy on a public URL (Cursor with your own OpenAI key, remote apps) (cont.)
chunks.text: request Cursor makes with your key now passes through the proxy: deduped, stale tool results trimmed, base64 stripped, real usage counted in `/t/<token>/stats`. This is the one Cursor path that is model-independent and needs no hook. It applies only to BYO-key traffic; Cursor's own

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically > Putting the proxy on a public URL (Cursor with your own OpenAI key, remote apps) (cont.)
chunks.text: subscription models never leave Cursor's servers.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically > Putting the proxy on a public URL (Cursor with your own OpenAI key, remote apps)
chunks.text: Your API key still rides in the request headers, as before. The token protects the relay, not the key; keep the tunnel HTTPS.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically > Putting the proxy on a public URL (Cursor with your own OpenAI key, remote apps)
chunks.text: > **Note on desktop chat apps:** Claude Desktop and the ChatGPT app talk to their own backends — no tool can sit in that path. For those, use the MCP integration below (Claude Desktop gets the standing rules and a cheap `profile_context` sketch call) and `context-doctor instructions

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Always-on: optimize every request automatically > Putting the proxy on a public URL (Cursor with your own OpenAI key, remote apps) (cont.)
chunks.text: --copy` for the per-account preferences.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps
chunks.text: ## Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps
chunks.text: `context-doctor` ships an MCP server, so the AI itself can profile and slim context on demand. Before the setup table, the honest question: **on which surfaces does it act by itself, and on which does it only nudge?** MCP gives a server no way to see the conversation or intercept a turn;

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text: only a hook or a place in the data path can do that.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps
chunks.text:
| Surface | Runs by itself | What that means |
|---|---|---|

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text: | **Claude Code** | Yes: hook on every prompt, status line on every refresh | Past ~80k tokens the model receives hygiene guidance naming the largest waste; compaction is offered. Measured: 115 automatic checks, 48 warnings, across 32 sessions on one machine |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text: | **Cursor** | **Yes**, since 0.26: `install` adds a native `postToolUse` hook to `~/.cursor/hooks.json`; Cursor passes it the agent transcript, and its `additional_context` reaches the model | In a heavy chat, the agent gets hygiene guidance and the largest recoverable waste, once per

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text: 40% of growth. Cursor's transcript records tool calls but not their output, and keeps turns Cursor has since summarized, so the note gives the chat's accumulated size, with no window share or price. Corrected in 0.26: Cursor also runs Claude Code's hook, but as `beforeSubmitPrompt`,

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text:
whose output can only allow or block the prompt, so from 0.15 to 0.25 the guidance never reached Cursor's model |
| **API traffic through the proxy** | Yes: every request rewritten in flight | Fewer tokens, guaranteed, model not consulted |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text: | **Claude Desktop** | The standing instruction in every chat (we confirmed in the app bundle that Desktop's `LocalMcpServerManager` reads it), a one-click `context_checkup` prompt, and since 0.17 a `profile_context` the model can actually afford to call from chat | Until 0.17 the tool

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text: wanted the whole conversation as its argument, so calling it from chat meant re-typing 50k tokens; nobody did, and Desktop's log showed zero calls in a month. Now the model passes a ~120-token **sketch** (turn count, the large or repeated blocks) and gets a sized estimate, findings and

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text: the fix to apply. Still a nudge, not a hook: Desktop chat has no hook API and no transcript on disk |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text: | **Codex (OpenAI): ChatGPT.app's Codex tab, the Codex IDE extension, the `codex` CLI** | **Yes**, since 0.16: `install` writes the hook to `~/.codex/hooks.json`, the MCP server to `~/.codex/config.toml`, and the skill to `~/.codex/skills/`. Codex uses Claude Code's hook contract almost

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text: verbatim and passes its own rollout transcript, which carries the API's real usage figures | Same guidance as Claude Code, from measured tokens. One extra step, Codex's rule not ours: a new hook runs only after you trust it once (type `/hooks` in Codex). The MCP tools are marked

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text:
read-only, so Codex runs them without an approval prompt, `codex exec` included. `session` and `session --list` read Codex rollouts too |
| **ChatGPT chat UI** | No | No MCP, no hooks, no data path in the chat product itself. Use Codex, or a developer-mode connector at a URL you host |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps
chunks.text: So "every chat inherently better" is true for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and the proxy; for Claude Desktop it is "the rules ride in every chat and the checkup is one cheap tool call away"; and not a claim we make for the ChatGPT chat UI.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps
chunks.text: **Where there is no hook and no MCP at all** (claude.ai on the web, the Claude and ChatGPT phone apps, plain ChatGPT): the app's per-account preferences are read on every turn, which is the closest those surfaces have to a hook. `context-doctor instructions --copy` puts the ~180-token

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text: rules on your clipboard and tells you where to paste them (claude.ai Settings > General; ChatGPT Settings > Personalization > Custom instructions, "What traits should ChatGPT have?").

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps
chunks.text:
**Do you need to configure anything by hand? Usually no:**

| App | Setup |
|---|---|

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text: | Claude Desktop | `npx context-doctor install` writes the config — just restart the app. Or one click: download `context-doctor-<version>.mcpb` from the [latest release](https://github.com/KushalP1/context-doctor/releases) and open it (Settings > Extensions). The bundle runs on

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text:
Desktop's own Node, no npm needed |
| Claude Code | Same command — MCP + skill + every-prompt hook, all automatic |
| Cursor | Same command — writes `~/.cursor/mcp.json` and the after-tool-call hook in `~/.cursor/hooks.json`. `context-doctor doctor` checks both |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text: | Codex (OpenAI) | Same command — `~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.codex/hooks.json`, `~/.codex/skills/`. Then, once, `/hooks` in Codex to trust the hook |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps (cont.)
chunks.text: | ChatGPT (developer mode) | **Manual + a reachable URL** — ChatGPT connects to servers over the internet, never local commands. Run `context-doctor-mcp --http` on a host/tunnel, then add the URL as a connector. Normal ChatGPT (no dev mode) has no MCP — use the CLI |

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps
context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps > How it works in Claude Desktop, step by step
chunks.text:
### How it works in Claude Desktop, step by step

1. Run `npx context-doctor install` (writes the config above for you) and restart Claude Desktop. Or open the `.mcpb` from the latest release: same server, no npm, installs as an Extension.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps > How it works in Claude Desktop, step by step (cont.)
chunks.text: 2. From then on, **every conversation carries context-doctor's standing instructions**. The MCP server hands them to Desktop on connect and Desktop puts them in front of Claude: summarize big pastes instead of re-quoting them, refer to earlier content by name, never inline base64, and

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps > How it works in Claude Desktop, step by step (cont.)
chunks.text: past ~30 turns or on any question about tokens, cost, speed or limits, call `profile_context` before answering.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps > How it works in Claude Desktop, step by step (cont.)
chunks.text: 3. That call is cheap on purpose. Claude cannot export a Desktop chat, so it passes a **sketch**: how many turns, which blocks are large, repeated, stale or images, with one size hint each (~120 tokens). The server sizes it (usually within ±20%, measured; see "Why token counts are ~"),

chunks.text:
### How it works in ChatGPT, step by step (honest version)

ChatGPT's MCP support differs fundamentally from Claude Desktop's: **it never spawns local processes**. Its custom connectors (developer mode) have OpenAI's servers connect to a **URL** — so the MCP server must be reachable from the internet.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps > How it works in ChatGPT, step by step (honest version)
chunks.text: 1. **Normal ChatGPT (no developer mode): no MCP at all.** context-doctor still helps via the CLI: export the conversation and run `npx context-doctor analyze chat.json --model gpt-5` / `optimize` — no account settings required.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps > How it works in ChatGPT, step by step (honest version) (cont.)
chunks.text: 2. **ChatGPT developer mode**: run our HTTP transport somewhere reachable — `context-doctor-mcp --http --port 8808` on a small host (bind `--host 0.0.0.0` there), or expose your machine temporarily with a tunnel (`ngrok http 8808`). Then Settings → Connectors → Advanced → Developer mode

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps > How it works in ChatGPT, step by step (honest version) (cont.)
chunks.text: → add connector with URL `https://<your-host>/mcp`.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps > How it works in ChatGPT, step by step (honest version) (cont.)
chunks.text:
3. Once connected, GPT gets the same three tools, each marked read-only (they only read their input and return text), with the same trigger guidance: ask *"what's eating my context?"* → it calls `profile_context`; *"optimize it"* works the same, including GPT writing the pruning summary 
itself.

chunks.heading: context-doctor 🩺 > Use with the Claude & ChatGPT apps > How it works in ChatGPT, step by step (honest version)
chunks.text: Security note for step 2: the HTTP endpoint is unauthenticated — put it behind your tunnel's auth or a reverse proxy if it stays up long-term.

Your local MCP server can't reach the website, but the behavior can. Two options: `context-doctor instructions --copy` and paste into Settings > General > personal preferences (applies everywhere you are signed in, phone included), or upload `skills/context-doctor/SKILL.md` under

chunks.heading: Pack: put only the parts of a document that matter into the context.
chunks.text:
/**
 * Pack: put only the parts of a document that matter into the context.
 *
 * Everything else in context-doctor slims a conversation after the fact. The
 * cheapest token is the one that never goes in: a 60k-token manual pasted to
 * answer one question costs 60k tokens on that message and on every message
 * after it. Pack splits files into chunks along their own structure (markdown
 * headings, top-level code declarations, paragraphs), ranks the chunks against
 * a question with BM25, and returns the best ones that fit a token budget, with
 * an id and line range on each so the model can ask for more.
 *
 * Offline and keyless like the rest of the tool: lexical ranking, no embeddings
 * and no model calls. Lexical ranking misses pure paraphrase; the outline that
 * comes with every result lets the model pick sections by heading when it does.
 */

**What it does to each request:** once old tool output adds up to 20k+ tokens (file reads, shell output, search and web results, screenshots inside them), it replaces that output with a one-line note, keeping the 3 most recent results. The tool call stays in the history, so the model can simply run it again if it needs the output. Your messages, its answers, answers you gave to its questions, subagent reports and MCP results are never touched.

**Why it cannot make a session more expensive.** A prompt cache matches a byte-identical prefix, and changing old history re-bills everything after the change at the write rate (1.25x instead of 0.1x). So autopilot changes history only when the cache is cold anyway: after an idle gap longer than the cache lifetime the request itself declares (1 hour for Claude Code on a subscription, 5 minutes otherwise), when the whole prompt is re-written regardless. Once cleared, an output stays cleared on every later request, so the prefix is identical between clearings and the cache keeps hitting.
